input_signals.name: Inventory-Reset Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(sale, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), INDICATOR(NEG(ACCEL(RATIO(invt, sale))), 0))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheap firms whose inventory accumulation is decelerating outperform expensive firms undergoing the same investment reset.
input_signals.reasoning: Sales yield is activated only when inventory intensity has begun to decelerate, indicating restraint after a working-capital build. This condition helps distinguish disciplined normalization from firms that remain cheap while continuing to invest aggressively in inventory.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( ratio( sale, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), indicator( neg( accel( ratio( invt, sale ) ) ), 0 ) )

input_signals.name: Scalable Labor Value
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), IND_RANK(SUB(GROWTH(sale, 1), GROWTH(emp, 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheap firms growing sales faster than headcount earn higher returns because the market underappreciates their investment-efficient scalability.
input_signals.reasoning: The second leg rewards demand growth achieved without commensurate labor investment, rather than indiscriminately favoring shrinking firms. The bottleneck construction requires both an attractive EBITDA yield and evidence of disciplined organizational expansion.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( ebitda, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), ind_rank( sub( growth( sale, 1 ), growth( emp, 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Capital-Plan Stability Spread
input_signals.expression: SUB(MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(sale, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), IND_RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(capx, at), 3)))), MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho), sale)), IND_RANK(VOL(RATIO(capx, at), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheap firms with stable capital programs outperform expensive firms with volatile capital programs.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the canonical book-to-market and asset-growth pairing with an interaction between valuation and investment-policy uncertainty. The two-sided construction targets disciplined, predictably investing value firms against richly priced firms whose unstable capital commitments make growth expectations less credible.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( min( ind_rank( ratio( sale, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), ind_rank( neg( vol( ratio( capx, at ), 3 ) ) ) ), min( ind_rank( ratio( mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ), sale ) ), ind_rank( vol( ratio( capx, at ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Productive-Capital Cash Value
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oancf, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(sale, ppent), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: High-cash-flow-yield firms with improving fixed-capital productivity earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The investment leg measures improvement in sales generated per unit of PP&E rather than rewarding low capex mechanically. The bottleneck requires both cheap cash generation and evidence that deployed productive assets are becoming more effective.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( oancf, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), ind_rank( delta( ratio( sale, ppent ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Priced Capacity Overhang
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho), sale)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(SUB(GROWTH(ppent, 1), GROWTH(sale, 1)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Expensive firms whose productive capacity grows faster than sales underperform as optimistic demand expectations fail to absorb the added capacity.
input_signals.reasoning: The investment leg measures a capacity-absorption gap rather than generic asset growth or external financing. Using PP&E and sales preserves broad coverage, while the conjunction isolates richly valued firms whose physical expansion is not yet supported by realized demand.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ), sale ) ), ind_rank( winsor( sub( growth( ppent, 1 ), growth( sale, 1 ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Scalable Value Gate
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), INDICATOR(IND_ZSCORE(SUB(GROWTH(sale, 1), GROWTH(emp, 1))), 0))
input_signals.hypothesis: EBITDA yield predicts returns more strongly among firms achieving above-industry sales growth relative to headcount growth.
input_signals.reasoning: The prior labor-scalability signal had the strongest cross-sectional evidence but weak portfolio alpha, potentially because its MIN construction placed firms failing either leg in the short tail. This gate neutralizes non-scalable firms and forms the valuation spread only where operating scalability confirms disciplined labor investment.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( ratio( ebitda, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), indicator( ind_zscore( sub( growth( sale, 1 ), growth( emp, 1 ) ) ), 0 ) )

input_signals.name: Stable-Budget Value Gate
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(sale, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), INDICATOR(NEG(IND_ZSCORE(VOL(RATIO(capx, at), 3))), 0))
input_signals.hypothesis: Sales yield is positively associated with returns among firms maintaining below-industry volatility in capital-expenditure intensity.
input_signals.reasoning: The prior stability spread had a positive Fama-MacBeth slope but significantly negative FF5 alpha, suggesting that explicitly shorting expensive, volatile investors created an adverse tail portfolio. This version retains investment stability as a credibility condition while neutralizing volatile firms instead of forcing them into the short leg.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( ratio( sale, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), indicator( neg( ind_zscore( vol( ratio( capx, at ), 3 ) ) ), 0 ) )

input_signals.name: Realized Reinvestment Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), INDICATOR(MIN(IND_ZSCORE(GROWTH(sale, 1)), IND_ZSCORE(LAG(RATIO(capx, at), 1))), 0))
input_signals.hypothesis: Among firms where substantial prior investment is followed by strong sales growth, cheap EBITDA yield predicts higher returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the inventory-change anomaly and problematic two-sided quadrant construction with a realized investment-payback mechanism. Requiring both above-industry lagged capex intensity and subsequent sales growth prevents the signal from mechanically rewarding low investment.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( ratio( ebitda, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), indicator( min( ind_zscore( growth( sale, 1 ) ), ind_zscore( lag( ratio( capx, at ), 1 ) ) ), 0 ) )

input_signals.name: Rejuvenated-Asset Value Gate
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), INDICATOR(IND_ZSCORE(DELTA(RATIO(ppent, ppegt), 1)), 0))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cash-generative cheap firms whose productive asset base is becoming newer earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Improvement in net-to-gross PP&E captures selective modernization or retirement of obsolete capital rather than low total-asset growth. Conditioning on operating-cash-flow yield helps distinguish funded asset rejuvenation from distressed balance-sheet contraction.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( ratio( oancf, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), indicator( ind_zscore( delta( ratio( ppent, ppegt ), 1 ) ), 0 ) )

input_signals.name: Goldilocks Investment Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ceq, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), SUB(INDICATOR(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, at), 5), 0.25), INDICATOR(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, at), 5), 0.75)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Book-to-market predicts returns most reliably when capex intensity is neither at a firm-specific investment trough nor at an aggressive peak.
input_signals.reasoning: The middle-history gate distinguishes disciplined normal investment from both empire-building peaks and potentially distressed maintenance troughs. It therefore tests whether avoiding investment extremes improves the value spread without mechanically loading on low cross-sectional investment.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( ratio( ceq, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), sub( indicator( ts_rank( ratio( capx, at ), 5 ), 0.25 ), indicator( ts_rank( ratio( capx, at ), 5 ), 0.75 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Capital-Optionality Cash Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), IND_RANK(RATIO(che, ADD(che, ppent))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Operating-cash-flow yield predicts higher returns more strongly when firms retain financial flexibility relative to irreversible tangible-capital commitments.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the archived cash-depletion and high-capex short with a capital-optionality mechanism based on the balance between liquid cash and installed PP&E. The bounded flexibility weight continuously strengthens the valuation spread without sparse temporal changes or mechanically forcing cash-burning firms into the short portfolio.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( ratio( oancf, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), ind_rank( ratio( che, add( che, ppent ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Capex-Backed Asset Renewal Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), MUL(IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(ppent, ppegt), 1)), IND_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppegt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheap cash-generative firms outperform when improvement in asset age is supported by meaningful renewal expenditure.
input_signals.reasoning: The net-to-gross PP&E change preserves the successful asset-age mechanism, while capex relative to gross PP&E helps distinguish active renewal from a ratio increase caused only by disposal of old assets. Continuous renewal weights preserve valuation ordering without adding another binary gate or claiming an unsupported coverage improvement.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( ratio( oancf, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), mul( ind_rank( delta( ratio( ppent, ppegt ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( capx, ppegt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Dual-Input Scalable Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), IND_RANK(MIN(SUB(GROWTH(sale, 1), GROWTH(emp, 1)), SUB(GROWTH(sale, 1), GROWTH(ppent, 1)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheap firms growing sales faster than both labor and fixed-capital inputs earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The strong labor-scalability evidence may still include firms substituting aggressive physical investment for headcount growth. Weighting valuation by the weaker of labor and PP&E scalability requires genuine output expansion without hidden growth in either major operating input.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( ratio( ebitda, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), ind_rank( min( sub( growth( sale, 1 ), growth( emp, 1 ) ), sub( growth( sale, 1 ), growth( ppent, 1 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Inventory-Absorption Cash Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), IND_RANK(RATIO(sale, ADD(sale, invt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheap cash-generative firms with little inventory tied up relative to sales earn higher returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The bounded sales-to-sales-plus-inventory ratio measures current working-capital absorption efficiency rather than the published inventory-change anomaly or a noisy inventory acceleration. It strengthens the valuation spread where cash generation is supported by limited capital lock-up in unsold goods.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( ratio( oancf, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), ind_rank( ratio( sale, add( sale, invt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Bounded Reinvestment Payback Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), IND_RANK(RATIO(DELTA(sale, 1), ADD(ABS(DELTA(sale, 1)), LAG(capx, 1)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cash-flow yield predicts higher returns when prior capital expenditure generates strong subsequent incremental sales.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the high-cash and low-leverage screen and instead measures realized payback on lagged investment. The bounded ratio avoids instability from dividing directly by small capex and distinguishes productive reinvestment from firms that merely spend aggressively.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( ratio( oancf, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), ind_rank( ratio( delta( sale, 1 ), add( abs( delta( sale, 1 ) ), lag( capx, 1 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Productive Renewal Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), MUL(IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(ppent, ppegt), 1)), IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(sale, ppent), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheap cash-generative firms outperform when asset rejuvenation is accompanied by improving fixed-asset productivity.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the strained young-assets-plus-low-capex conjunction with two mutually reinforcing outcomes: a younger asset base and rising sales per unit of net PP&E. Continuous rank weights avoid creating a thinner hard-gated subset, while the productivity confirmation reduces exposure to generic HML and CMA tilts.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( ratio( oancf, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), mul( ind_rank( delta( ratio( ppent, ppegt ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( delta( ratio( sale, ppent ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Replacement-Cycle Valuation Risk
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho), sale)), MUL(IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(ppent, ppegt))), IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(capx, sale), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Expensive firms with old productive assets and a rising capex burden underperform as deferred replacement needs begin consuming cash flow.
input_signals.reasoning: This measures the replacement-burden mechanism directly through asset age and the subsequent increase in capex intensity, rather than through another cash-to-capital ratio. The interaction targets richly valued firms entering a costly renewal cycle, not firms that merely hold little cash.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( ratio( mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ), sale ) ), mul( ind_rank( neg( ratio( ppent, ppegt ) ) ), ind_rank( delta( ratio( capx, sale ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Persistent Workforce Productivity Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), IND_RANK(TREND(RATIO(sale, emp), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheap firms with sustained improvement in sales per employee earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Prior labor-scalability signals used a one-period growth gap and produced strong cross-sectional evidence but less reliable portfolio alpha. A multi-period productivity trend targets persistent organizational scalability rather than a single hiring pause or temporary sales spike.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( ratio( ebitda, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), ind_rank( trend( ratio( sale, emp ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Reliable Capacity-Utilization Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(sale, ppent)), IND_RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(sale, ppent), 3)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheap cash-generative firms with both high and stable utilization of productive capacity earn higher returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the archived capex-payback horizon construction and therefore avoids embedding multi-year sales momentum. Requiring both strong fixed-asset turnover and low turnover volatility distinguishes consistently efficient capital deployment from temporarily high utilization or inactive firms.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( ratio( oancf, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), mul( ind_rank( ratio( sale, ppent ) ), ind_rank( neg( vol( ratio( sale, ppent ), 3 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Backlog-Addressing Renewal Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), MIN(IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(ppent, ppegt))), IND_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppegt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheap cash-generative firms outperform when they actively reinvest in an old productive asset base.
input_signals.reasoning: An old asset stock and high renewal spending are economically complementary, unlike the strained young-assets-plus-low-capex pairing. This targets firms addressing a genuine replacement backlog and does not mechanically recombine the archived rejuvenation-change and cash-optionality weights.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( ratio( oancf, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), min( ind_rank( neg( ratio( ppent, ppegt ) ) ), ind_rank( ratio( capx, ppegt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Productive-Capital Recycling Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(capx, DELTA(ppegt, 1)), LAG(ppegt, 1)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheap profitable firms that actively retire or replace obsolete productive capital earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Capex minus the change in gross PP&E approximates capital retirements and replacement activity, creating a capital-recycling measure rather than an asset-growth or goodwill-impairment signal. EBITDA yield helps exclude asset-shedding firms lacking ongoing operating support, while winsorization limits accounting-reconciliation noise.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( ratio( ebitda, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( capx, delta( ppegt, 1 ) ), lag( ppegt, 1 ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Productive-Investment Mix Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(sale, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), IND_RANK(RATIO(capx, ADD(capx, MUL(DELTA(invt, 1), INDICATOR(DELTA(invt, 1), 0))))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheap firms allocating current investment toward productive fixed assets rather than positive inventory accumulation earn higher returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This measures the composition of investment flows rather than substituting inventory for labor in an output-scalability formula. The bounded share compares capex with contemporaneous positive inventory investment, targeting disciplined productive deployment without rewarding inventory liquidation mechanically.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( ratio( sale, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), ind_rank( ratio( capx, add( capx, mul( delta( invt, 1 ), indicator( delta( invt, 1 ), 0 ) ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Verified Capital Recycling Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(capx, DELTA(ppegt, 1)), LAG(ppegt, 1)), 1)), IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(ppent, ppegt), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheap profitable firms outperform when implied capital retirement is followed by observable rejuvenation of the productive asset base.
input_signals.reasoning: The capital-recycling proxy had very strong cross-sectional evidence but weaker portfolio alpha, plausibly because acquisitions, foreign exchange, and accounting reclassifications contaminate the gross-PP&E reconciliation. Requiring a concurrent improvement in net-to-gross PP&E verifies that the recycling activity actually produces a younger capital stock.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( ratio( ebitda, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), min( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( capx, delta( ppegt, 1 ) ), lag( ppegt, 1 ) ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( delta( ratio( ppent, ppegt ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Operating-Profit Payback Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), IND_RANK(RATIO(DELTA(ebitda, 1), ADD(ABS(DELTA(ebitda, 1)), LAG(capx, 1)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cash-flow-cheap firms outperform when prior capital expenditure produces strong incremental operating profit.
input_signals.reasoning: This is a controlled refinement of the successful bounded payback signal: only the payoff output changes from sales to EBITDA, while the empirically supported operating-cash-flow valuation anchor remains fixed. It therefore tests whether realized operating-profit creation improves on revenue payback without confounding the result with a weaker sales-yield anchor.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( ratio( oancf, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), ind_rank( ratio( delta( ebitda, 1 ), add( abs( delta( ebitda, 1 ) ), lag( capx, 1 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Funded Active-Investment Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(che, ADD(che, capx))), IND_RANK(RATIO(capx, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheap cash-generative firms earn higher returns when they can undertake meaningful investment without exhausting their liquidity reserves.
input_signals.reasoning: Cash relative to current capex measures funding capacity, while capex intensity requires that the firm is actually investing rather than appearing flexible because investment is negligible. Because capx enters the two legs in opposing directions, the weakest-link construction avoids the common-denominator asset-lightness bias of the rejected optionality overlay.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( ratio( oancf, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), min( ind_rank( ratio( che, add( che, capx ) ) ), ind_rank( ratio( capx, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Improving Total-Factor Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), MIN(IND_RANK(TREND(RATIO(sale, emp), 3)), IND_RANK(TREND(RATIO(sale, ppent), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheap firms with persistent improvement in both labor and fixed-capital productivity earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This reorients the mechanism toward the jointly favorable state rather than using a signed expensive-short score that inadvertently placed cheap deteriorators in an extreme portfolio. The weakest productivity trend limits the weight, so improvement in one input cannot conceal dilution in the other.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( ratio( ebitda, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), min( ind_rank( trend( ratio( sale, emp ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( trend( ratio( sale, ppent ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Demand-Triggered Investment Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), MIN(TS_RANK(RATIO(sale, ppent), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppegt), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheap cash-generative firms outperform when elevated capital expenditure occurs in response to high firm-specific capacity utilization.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the cosmetic workforce valuation-anchor swap with an investment-timing mechanism: capex is rewarded only when both utilization and renewal intensity are high relative to the firm’s own history. The interaction distinguishes demand-triggered expansion from indiscriminate high investment or generic low-capex conservatism.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( ratio( oancf, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), min( ts_rank( ratio( sale, ppent ), 5 ), ts_rank( ratio( capx, ppegt ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Liquidity-Covered Rejuvenation
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), MIN(IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(ppent, ppegt), 1)), IND_RANK(RATIO(che, ADD(che, capx)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheap cash-generative firms outperform when they rejuvenate productive assets while retaining liquidity relative to current investment spending.
input_signals.reasoning: The asset-age change confirms that meaningful renewal occurred, while cash relative to capex measures whether that renewal strained financial flexibility. Unlike the rejected optionality overlay, the two conditioning legs do not share PP&E as a denominator, and active rejuvenation prevents low capex alone from generating a high score.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( ratio( oancf, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), min( ind_rank( delta( ratio( ppent, ppegt ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( che, add( che, capx ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Persistent Fixed-Capital Earnings Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), IND_RANK(TREND(RATIO(ebitda, ppent), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheap cash-generative firms with persistently improving operating earnings per unit of net PP&E earn higher returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This measures the sustained earnings productivity of installed capital rather than capex level, asset growth, or one-period turnover changes. It extends the successful persistent-productivity evidence to a direct operating return on the productive asset stock.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( ratio( oancf, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), ind_rank( trend( ratio( ebitda, ppent ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Output-Verified Capital Recycling
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(capx, DELTA(ppegt, 1)), LAG(ppegt, 1)), 1)), IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(sale, ppent), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheap profitable firms outperform when capital retirement and replacement are accompanied by improving fixed-asset turnover.
input_signals.reasoning: The prior recycling signal had exceptionally strong cross-sectional evidence but more modest portfolio alpha, while its asset-age verification was partly mechanical.
